subject: Day 41: maternal 6-week postpartum visit tomorrow
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 41. Anoushka's 6-week postpartum visit is tomorrow. Today is for finalizing the question list, refreshing the EPDS, and packing what the visit needs.

Action items
- Anoushka: refresh the EPDS today and bring the result. Pelvic-floor symptoms, mood, return to exercise, contraception, breastfeeding plan, and return-to-work date are the typical agenda. Postpartum Support International: https://www.postpartum.net/
- Confirm transportation and childcare during the visit; one parent attending alone is fine if the question list is clear.
- Pack the question list, the EPDS score, the breastfeeding plan, and the contraception preference. ACOG on postpartum birth control: https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/postpartum-birth-control
- Confirm the 2-month well visit is booked. AAP Bright Futures periodicity: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Spontaneous smiles; vowel coos; turn-taking; head control sustained 30-60 seconds.
- [low concern] Crying near peak intensity in the evenings.
- [monitor] Persistent low mood, anxiety, or intrusive thoughts in Anoushka — say it at the visit explicitly.
- [call within 24h] Maternal heavy bleeding, large clots, or severe pain. For the baby: a cluster of poor feeding, lethargy, and decreased output.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunities
- Read aloud 15 minutes in a calm window. Reach Out and Read evidence base: https://reachoutandread.org/
- Lay him on a blanket on the grass for a few minutes of outdoor sensory input while you get some fresh air before tomorrow's visit. AAP HealthyChildren on infant senses: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/default.aspx
- Sing live during a routine; participation over performance. Gerry, Unrau, Trainor, Dev Sci 2012: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22490184/
- Take conversational turns with each vocalization. Romeo et al., Psych Science 2018: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29442613/

Upcoming
- Day 42: maternal 6-week postpartum visit.
- Day 49: crying typically tapering noticeably.
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit and first vaccines.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete

- Holds head up while on tummy
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained head lift of several seconds, not just a brief bob. Forearms may or may not be supporting yet.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-head-up-tummy/complete

- Hands relax open most of the time
  AAP window: day 35-90
  What to look for: Newborn fists relax as the palmar grasp reflex fades. Predictor of voluntary grasp coming.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/hands-open-mostly/complete

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete
